dedupe_keys.name: bailiwick of guernsey risk register civil contingencies authority

description: The Bailiwick Risk Register is the public strategic risk assessment of the Civil Contingencies Authority of the States of Guernsey, covering Guernsey, Alderney and Sark. The version read is version 8 with a review date of June 2014, a 20-page PDF. It explains that the Civil Contingencies (Bailiwick of Guernsey) Law, 2012 requires the Authority to maintain and update the register at least once a year, that it draws on UK risk assessment guidance, and that it follows six stages from contextualisation to monitoring and review. Each risk has a lead body, a description of the reasonable worst case and a rating, often with separate ratings for Alderney and Sark. Risks include pollution of controlled waters and potable abstraction points, fuel spills, accidents in the transport of fuel, a maritime accident restricting St Peter Port Harbour with effects on fuel supply, aviation accidents, storms and gales, coastal and tidal flooding that can flood sewage infrastructure, other flooding, building collapse with loss of power and essential services, and reservoir dam failure. Access is free as a public PDF; no licence is stated. Caveats: the edition read dates from 2014, and newer editions were not found on the page read. Coverage is the Bailiwick of Guernsey. It supports emergency planning and cascading failure scenarios for small island infrastructure; the related record is the UK National Risk Register.
